name: Sonnet deep value
strategy: Relative-value mean-reversion and low-vol carry harvesting: long defensive/oversold laggards, short parabolic momentum extensions, funded by cash carry.
novelty: Round 1 and 2 both bet on statistically cheap cyclical/value large-caps that stayed unloved through a melt-up. Round 3 abandons value entirely: the edge here is vol-regime mean reversion and carry harvesting — pairing long low-volatility/oversold names against short overextended momentum leaders (semis, mega-cap tech, BTC), while collecting funding-free short exposure and 4% cash APY. This is a relative-value/positioning trade, not a valuation thesis.

positions.thesis: Low-volatility quality factor lagging the melt-up (+5.8% 12m vs SPY +22.7%); harvests carry and offers ballast if momentum unwinds.
Low-vol carry sleeve, cheap ballast against short momentum book, minimal correlation to the crowded SMH/XLK trade.
Miners down -13.2%/1m and -24.3%/3m despite gold only -6%/-15% — oversold relative to bullion, mean-reversion bounce candidate.
Biotech showing accelerating relative strength (+14.6% 1m vs flat SPY) — momentum continuation catalyst distinct from prior cyclical/value themes.
Mega-cap tech showing first cracks (-5.2% 1m after +25.8%/6m) — short the extension as a mean-reversion hedge against the crowded long-momentum trade.
Semis parabolic at +103.8% 12m with a sharp -8.7% 1m reversal already underway — vol-regime overextension short.
BTC in a confirmed downtrend (-14.7%/3m, -32.9%/6m, -46%/12m); shorting the perp avoids the 10% APR funding drag that hits longs only.

outlook: Expect continued rotation out of the most extended AI/semis momentum trade and a partial mean-reversion bounce in beaten-down gold miners and defensive low-vol names, while crypto stays in a structural downtrend; biotech's fresh relative strength offers an independent momentum leg uncorrelated to the tech unwind.
